He has previously played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Chicago Bulls]], and [[Sacramento Kings]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Austin Peay Governors basketball|Austin Peay Governors]]. ==Early life== Taylor grew up in [[Bowling Green, Kentucky]] and attended Bowling Green High School. During his junior year, he averaged 15.3 points and 11.3 rebounds per game and was named second-team All-State. Taylor committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Austin Peay State University]] going into his senior year over offers from [[Texas Southern Tigers basketball|Texas Southern]] and [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State]].{{cite web|first=Elliott|last=Pratt|title=BG's Taylor verbally commits to Austin Peay|url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/prep/bg-s-taylor-verbally-commits-to-austin-peay/article_a6ad635e-455b-59ca-812c-62ec35ae0b38.html|work=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]]|date=August 29, 2016|access-date=March 4, 2020}} As a senior, Taylor averaged 17.7 points and 11.8 rebounds per game and was named first team All-State and the MVP of the Kentucky Sweet 16 after averaging 20.5 points and 10 rebounds where he led Bowling Green to its first state title, alongside [[Zion Harmon]], former consensus four-star recruit in the class of 2021. Taylor scored 1,704 points and grabbed 1,300 rebounds over four seasons with Bowling Green.{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Frakes|title=C-J All-State basketball: Terry Taylor|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2017/04/14/c-j-all-state-basketball-terry-taylor/100464090/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=April 14, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2020}} ==College career== As a true freshman, Taylor averaged 15.6 points and 8.6 rebounds per game and was named the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) Freshman of the Year and first team All-OVC.{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Burgess|title=Austin Peay Basketball: Terry Taylor and Dayton Gumm to lead the Governors for 2018-19|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2018/11/03/austin-peay-basketball-terry-taylor-dayton-gumm-lead-governors-2018-19/|website=BustingBrackets.com|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=March 4, 2020}} As a sophomore he averaged 20.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game and was again named first team All-OVC.{{cite web|title=Austin Peay's Taylor picked as Preseason OVC Player of the Year|url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/austin-peay-s-taylor-picked-as-preseason-ovc-player-of/article_6c63931d-61ec-55ff-80d4-4ef402f07d8a.html|work=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]]|date=October 18, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2020}}{{cite web|title=Austin Peay State University Basketball's Terry Taylor, Carlos Paez awarded OVC Weekly honors|url=https://www.clarksvilleonline.com/2020/01/14/austin-peay-state-university-basketballs-terry-taylor-carlos-paez-awarded-ovc-weekly-honors|work=Clarksville Online|date=January 14, 2020|access-date=March 4, 2020}} He scored the 1,000th point of his college career during the season as part of a 25-point, 12-rebound performance in a win over [[2018–19 Eastern Illinois Panthers men's basketball team|Eastern Illinois]] on February 9, 2019.{{cite web|first=Colby|last=Wilson|title=Taylor reaches 1,000 points as Govs avenge earlier loss to EIU|url=https://clarksvillenow.com/local/taylor-reaches-1000-points-as-govs-avenge-earlier-loss-to-eiu/|website=ClarksvilleNow.com|date=February 9, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2020}} Taylor's career-high 39 points came on December 17, in an 80–61 win over [[McKendree Bearcats|McKendree]].{{cite news|title=Taylor scores 39 to lift Austin Peay past McKendree 80-61|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401173881|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 17, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2020}} On January 23, 2020, Taylor hit a career-high six three-pointers and had 37 points and 14 rebounds in a 99–74 win over [[2019–20 Tennessee State Tigers basketball team|Tennessee State]].{{cite news|first=George|last=Robinson|title=Austin Peay Govs 99, Tennessee State 74: 5 things we learned|url=https://www.theleafchronicle.com/story/sports/2020/01/23/austin-peays-jordyn-adams-terry-taylor-pour-37-each-win/4521698002/|work=[[Clarksville Leaf-Chronicle]]|date=January 24, 2020|access-date=March 4, 2020}} Taylor was named the [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and first team All-OVC for a third straight season as a junior after averaging 21.8 points, 11.0 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|title=Austin Peay's Terry Taylor is OVC basketball player of the year; 3 Belmont players honored|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2020/03/03/austin-peays-terry-taylor-ovc-player-year-3-belmont-players-first-team/4926109002/|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=March 3, 2020|access-date=March 4, 2020}}{{cite web|title=APSU Basketball's Terry Taylor named USBWA All-District|url=https://www.clarksvilleonline.com/2020/03/10/apsu-basketballs-terry-taylor-named-usbwa-all-district/|website=ClarksvilleOnline.com|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 13, 2020}} Following the season, Taylor declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], but maintained his college eligibility, ultimately returning for his senior year.{{cite news|title=Former Purple star Taylor declares for NBA draft|url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/former-purple-star-taylor-declares-for-nba-draft/article_36fda15a-1cef-5d5d-a12d-2e80ebf50e3e.html|work=[[Bowling Green Daily News]]|date=April 18, 2020|access-date=April 21, 2020|archive-date=April 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200419175306/https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/former-purple-star-taylor-declares-for-nba-draft/article_36fda15a-1cef-5d5d-a12d-2e80ebf50e3e.html|url-status=dead}} On December 5, 2020, Taylor surpassed the 2,000-career-point mark, scoring 10 points in a 102–38 win against [[Carver College]].{{cite news|title=Taylor tops 2000 in dominating home win|url=https://letsgopeay.com/news/2020/12/4/mens-basketball-taylor-tops-2000-in-dominating-home-win.aspx|website=LetsGoPeay.com|publisher=[[Austin Peay Governors]]|date=December 5, 2020|access-date=December 5, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants / Indiana Pacers (2021–2023)=== After not being selected in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Taylor signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]] on August 5, 2021.{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Keller|title=Pacers Sign Washington Jr., Sykes, Taylor|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-washington-jr-sykes-taylor|website=NBA.com|date=August 5, 2021|access-date=August 5, 2021}} He played for the Pacers during the [[2021 NBA Summer League]], but was waived on October 15.{{cite web|title=Pacers Announce Roster Moves - Oct. 15, 2021|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-announce-roster-moves-oct-15-2021|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}} Nine days later, he joined the [[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite tweet|author=Fort Wayne Mad Ants|title=Here is a look at our 2021 Training Camp roster as we tip things off on Monday! It is time. #15YearsGold #MadAntTrainingCamp 😡🐜🏀|number=1452342408159666185|user=TheMadAnts|date=October 24, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}} After 11 games for Fort Wayne, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with Indiana on December 15, 2021. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Pacers and the Mad Ants.{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Jarreau, Sign Taylor to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-jarreau-sign-taylor-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}} On February 2, 2022, in his seventh NBA game against the [[Orlando Magic]], Taylor subbed in 22 seconds into the game and stepped up as the Pacers' center. He recorded career highs of 24 points, 16 rebounds and 3 assists in 37 minutes for his first career double-double.{{cite web|title=Magic vs. Pacers - Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401360592|website=ESPN.com|date=February 2, 2022|access-date=April 7, 2022}} On April 7, 2022, the Pacers converted his two-way contract into a standard one.{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Terry Taylor And Duane Washington, Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-taylor-washington-jr|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=April 7, 2022}} In 18 games for Fort Wayne during the [[2021–22 NBA G League season]], Taylor averaged 21.3 points, 11.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.5 steals per game.{{cite web|title=Terry Taylor Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Terry-Taylor/Summary/121779|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 15, 2021}} Taylor played for the Pacers during the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]. After fives games with Fort Wayne{{cite web |title=Terry Taylor G-League Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/t/taylote01d.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=21 January 2026 |language=en}} and 26 games with Indiana during the [[2022–23 Indiana Pacers season|2022–23 season]],{{cite web |title=Terry Taylor Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/taylote01.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=21 January 2026 |language=en}} he was waived by the Pacers on February 9, 2023.{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Acquire Jordan Nwora, George Hill, and Serge Ibaka, and Multiple Second-Round Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-jordan-nwora-george-hill-serge-ibaka-multiple-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}} ===Chicago / Windy City Bulls (2023–2024)=== On February 22, 2023, Taylor signed a two-way contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Terry Taylor to a two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-terry-taylor-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2023|access-date=January 22, 2023}} He played seven games with the [[Windy City Bulls]] to finish the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]], while also playing five games for Chicago to finish the [[2022–23 Chicago Bulls season|2022–23 NBA season]]. On August 14, 2023, Taylor signed a standard contract with Chicago.{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls sign Terry Taylor|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-sign-terry-taylor|website=NBA.com|date=August 14, 2023|access-date=August 15, 2023}} He was waived on April 4, 2024.{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls sign Javonte Green|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-sign-javonte-green|website=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=April 4, 2024}} Taylor played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]. ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2024–2025)=== On September 23, 2024, Taylor signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]],{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Terry Taylor|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-terry-taylor|website=NBA.com|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=September 25, 2024}} but was waived on October 18.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-roster-moves-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}} On October 27, he joined the [[Stockton Kings]] for the [[2024–25 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} On March 18, 2025, he signed a 10-day contract with Sacramento.{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign Terry Taylor to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-terry-taylor-to-10-day-contract|access-date=March 23, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} He appeared in three NBA games, and following the expiration of his 10-day contract, he returned to Stockton. ===Brisbane Bullets (2025–2026)=== On July 14, 2025, Taylor signed a one-year contract with the [[Ningbo Rockets]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web | last=Maher | first=Rory | title=Terry Taylor Signs With Chinese Team | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2025-07-14 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/terry-taylor-signs-with-chinese-team.html | access-date=2025-12-13}} On November 15, his contract was terminated.{{cite web |title=宁波男篮：特里·泰勒身体情况未达俱乐部要求 球队已与其解约 |url=https://news.zhibo8.com/nba/2025-11-15/691854b4e2127native.htm |website=直播吧 |access-date=November 17, 2025 |date=November 15, 2025}} On December 1, 2025, Taylor signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the rest of the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]].{{cite news |title=Bullets sign high-impact NBA forward Terry Taylor |url=https://www.brisbanebullets.com.au/news/bullets-sign-high-impact-nba-forward-terry-taylor |access-date=1 December
